# `bin/annotate-claim`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/annotate-claim`](../../../bin/annotate-claim)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/annotate-claim C-NNN "text" [--dry-run]  ·  bin/annotate-claim --batch FILE [--dry-run]

Appends a note to CLAIMS.md for an existing entry (LESSONS.md "A changed novelty or an audit finding", 2026-09-16):

    ## C-049-note  2026-09-16  <text>

CLAIMS.md is append-only, so this is the only way to record something about a claim after the
fact WITHOUT changing its truth: novelty status found later (an entry turns out to be a known result), an audit
finding on the artifact's coverage or wording, a pointer to a later run.
A changed truth is not a note: it is a new claim that `supersedes` the old one. bin/merge,
bin/ledger-claims and bin/close-run print existing notes for an id they touch.
Refused: an id with no `## C-NNN  [TAG]` header, an empty text, text with a `## ` line in it,
no valid user approval (LESSONS.md "Every launch and every ledger append consumes a byte-bound": `bin/approve --annotate C-NNN "text"` with exactly this
text, within 30 minutes, CLAIMS.md unchanged since; consumed by the append). --operator-approved is
still accepted and means nothing.
LESSONS.md "A note says whose it is and does not vouch for the entry": a note is the orchestrator's, and no referee reads it,
so it may not vouch for the entry: text saying that the entry's truth is unchanged is refused (before
the approval is touched), and every note is appended with the fixed ending NOTE_SUFFIX.
--batch FILE: several notes from a JSON list of {id, text}, on one approval (`bin/approve --annotate-batch FILE`,
every note printed in full), appended in one write, all or none (LESSONS.md "One approval for several notes").
--dry-run: every check except the approval; prints the line that would be appended; appends nothing.
Use it before offering the approval, so a refused text never costs one.
```
